subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.

spec.name: Warhound 2077 Militarized Hauler
spec.description: A low-poly cyberpunk armoured six-wheeled military truck with an angular cab, neon trim, roof turret and a modular cargo bed, built from many small detail parts.
spec.layout: A long, low, wedge-nosed six-wheel (3 axles) heavy truck facing +Z. Front: sloped armoured hood with a light bar and a grille wedge, then a tall angular two-door cab with slanted glass and a roof-mounted remote turret at the cab rear. Behind the cab sits a flat armoured cargo bed (a container with ribbed panels, hazard stripes, antenna masts and rear ramp lights). Wheels are chunky octagonal low-poly tyres with glowing hub rings, partly covered by angular fender armour. Dark gunmetal hull, hazard-yellow trim, magenta and cyan neon strips along the skirts and cab edges, orange tail lights. Everything uses faceted, blocky primitives with small layered details (rivets, vents, panel lines, decals as thin parts). The floor is touched only by the six tyres.

parts.builds: Frame and underbody: twin longitudinal girders, cross members, armoured belly plate, fuel and battery tanks with strapping, drive shafts, differentials at three axles, exhaust stacks with orange glowing tips, side skirts with magenta and cyan neon strips, skirt panel lines and rivets, tow hooks and front bumper wedge with a cyan under-glow bar, rear bumper with tail lights and a tow hitch. Colours: hullDark, armor, steel, trim hazard stripes on bumpers, neon strips.
parts.attaches: Top face at chassisTop carries cab, cargo and hood; axle lines at frontAxle, midAxle, rearAxle feed the running gear; parent joint body.

parts.builds: Six chunky octagonal faceted tyres with tread blocks as small parts, rims with bolt rings, glowing cyan hub rings and centre caps, suspension arms, leaf spring stacks, shock absorbers with coil springs, brake discs, angular fender armour arches over each wheel with hazard-yellow edge trim and rivets, mud flaps with decal strips. Wheel radius 0.6 so tyres touch y = 0; track half-width 1.2 with tyre width 0.5.
parts.attaches: Wheels ride joints wheelFL, wheelFR, wheelML, wheelMR, wheelRL, wheelRR at the axle mounts; fenders and suspension attach to chassis girders along chassisTop.

parts.builds: Sloped wedge hood from hoodFront back to the cab, with vents, a grille of dark slats with a cyan glowing strip, twin angular headlights (headWhite glowing) with magenta DRL bars, a roof light bar with orange amber lamps, a bull-bar armour grille in hull with trim hazard chevrons, a winch drum on the bumper. Tall angular cab with armoured slanted windscreen, side windows with glassGlint reflections as thin parts, doors with panel lines, handles and rivets, armour add-on plates, wing mirrors with small screens, a roof hatch, roof antennas and sensor domes, a dashboard visible through glass with screenGreen displays, cab edge neon trim in cyan and magenta, and a unit emblem decal made of small parts.
parts.attaches: Sits on chassisTop at cabFloor; back wall meets cargoFront at z about 0.1 and the roof top at turretRing y 3.0 provides the turret mount; joint cab.

parts.builds: Remote weapon station on the cab-rear roof at turretRing: a rotating octagonal ring base with teeth and rivets, an angular armoured housing with sensor eye cluster (cyan glowing lenses), twin autocannon barrels with muzzle brakes, ammo box with a feed belt of small brass bullets (trim), a missile pod with four tubes on the side, a radar dish on a mast, status lights in warnOrange and magenta, hazard stripes and a number decal. Gun barrels point +Z. Entire assembly is about 1.1 m wide and 0.9 m tall above the ring.
parts.attaches: Base ring sits at turretRing on the cab roof; rides turretYaw and gunPitch.

parts.builds: Armoured container behind the cab from cargoFront to the tail: a floor deck on cargoFloor, ribbed side panels with recessed panel lines, a roof with vents, solar panels and antenna masts with blinking lights, roll-up side hatches with handles, hazard stripe bands and warning decals, stacked ammo crates and fuel drums strapped on a rear roof rack, a tall radio mast with cyan glowing tip, a rear ramp door on rampHinge with locking bars, hydraulic arms, tail light clusters in tailRed and warnOrange, a license plate and holographic unit logo in magenta and cyan. Colours: hull, hullLight, olive crates, rust drums, trim stripes.
parts.attaches: Deck sits on chassisTop and cargoFloor; front face meets cab back at cargoFront; rear ramp on rampHinge; joints body and rampHinge.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning the chassis builder, setting up helper functions for boxes and cylinders attached to bones, keeping it efficient while using a glow kit for neon accents.

I'm now working out the geometry for the girders, wheel wells, and skirt panels, checking that spacing between wheels at different z-positions doesn't collide and that skirt panels fill gaps between axles appropriately. I'm structuring this with loops for cross members and flange plates, aiming for around 120 parts total.

Next I'm planning the belly plate dimensions and fuel tank/battery placements, positioning cylindrical tanks outside the girders between the wheel wells with straps to secure them.

Still placing exhaust stacks vertically near the cab with glowing tips, then moving to skirt panels with neon strips and rivets, plus front tow hooks and a wedge-shaped bumper geometry.

Adding hazard stripes and under-glow bar, then building the rear bumper with tail lights and a hitch assembly, using degree-based rotation for the tilted bumper piece.

I'm sketching a cargo bed builder function, keeping it organized while using loosely typed parameters for the box geometry and bone structures since the exact context type isn't imported.

Now I'm laying out the structure in detail: a deck slab, main container walls spanning y1.5-2.85 with a roof cap, side ribs running along the length, recessed panel lines, and roll-up hatches, all positioned relative to a rear hinge for the ramp door.

Still placing accessories: hazard stripe bands near the base, a triangular warning decal, roof vents, solar panels with grid lines, blinking antenna lights, a rear roof rack with crates and rust-colored drums, and a tall radio mast with a glowing tip.

I need to keep everything within the height limit of 3.1, so I'm adjusting the container to span roughly y 1.5 to 2.6 with its roof just above that, letting the rack crates reach toward 3.0 and the mast tip sit right at the ceiling. Now I'm sizing the rear ramp door as a flat panel near the back edge.

Adding the locking bars and hydraulic hinge cylinders on either side of the ramp, plus corner tail lights (red and orange), a license plate with dark text bars, and small magenta/cyan hologram logo shapes on the side panels. I'm also sketching a small front panel with a cable conduit detail, then writing helper functions to generate these pieces with rotation handling for angled cylinders.

I'm planning the cabHood function with box geometry, using flat colors and defining the chassis and cab dimensions with specific coordinate ranges.

Working out the hood wedge shape next: I'll use an extruded outline along the z-axis to create the sloping front, mapping out side-view points for the roofline tapering down toward the front bumper.

Now I'm shaping the cab body and greenhouse as a lower box plus a narrower slanted upper section, building the greenhouse as an extruded profile with points tracing the roofline from windscreen to rear, then I'll add the glass separately.

For the windscreen, I'm computing the slope angle between the roof and the base point (about 34.7°) and working out the rotation needed about the X-axis so a thin box tilts forward correctly to match that slant, settling on a negative rotation angle.

Now I'm sizing and offsetting the glass panel along its normal, then placing thin side window boxes at the cab's sides with appropriate z-range and height. For glints I'm using rotated diagonal strips on the yz-plane, and then moving on to door seams, rivets, and lower armor plating details before planning mirror placement.

Mirrors with green screens, plus cyan/magenta neon trim along the roof and lower cab edges. I'm realizing the dashboard and interior would be hidden behind the solid extruded greenhouse hull, so I'm reconsidering the structure — making the interior a recessed dark box inset from the outer glass shell so the dashboard and pillars can actually be visible through the windows instead of buried inside solid geometry.

I'll settle this: make side windows glass only on the upper 55%, leaving the lower portion open so the interior is actually visible through a gap instead of fully obscured.

Then I need to build the greenhouse structure itself—pillars, roof, and glass panels at the sides—plus interior elements like the back wall, floor, seats, and a dashboard with screens facing the driver that are partly visible from the side.

Now I'm moving to the hood and front details: wedge-shaped hood with vents, a scoop, and a grille with dark slats and a cyan glow strip. I'm adding angular headlights with glowing white and magenta DRLs, a bull bar with chevron trim, and working out where to place a cylindrical winch drum under the grille relative to the chassis height.

Pulling the front face back to z4.1 with the bull bar extending to 4.3 instead. Now I'm positioning roof details: a light bar on the front roof edge with amber lamps, a roof hatch, rear antenna sensors, and working around the turret mount to keep the ring area clear.

Placing rear corner antenna domes, then adding neon trim rods along the roof's cab edges in cyan and along the lower cab in magenta, extending up through the A-pillars. For the door emblem I'm setting up a rotated hexagonal cylinder with inner bar accents in yellow and magenta, aligning it to the door surface and sketching the lower cab panel lines.

Still planning door outlines...

Working out wheel arch dimensions for the front wheels and confirming fender placement belongs to the running gear module. Setting up helper functions for boxes and glow effects, and thinking through an extra color palette entry before moving into extrusion geometry.

Calculating the hood's slope angle and resulting rotation for the vent slats, then working out the windscreen's tilt angle relative to the roofline.

Now I'm sizing the cab lower body to overlap properly with the hood, then working out the roof slab dimensions with a sloping visor overhang at the front.

For the interior I'm placing a dark box for the back wall, with the cab top serving as the floor, then adding seats and a dashboard with glowing green screens. I'm also positioning the side window panes and glass strips, plus the A-pillar as a thin angled box connecting the roofline to the body.

Now I'm adding B and C pillars at the side, a sill beam along the bottom, and working out mirror placement constrained by the box width limits -- settling on mounting them near the front of the A-pillars with a small glowing screen on the back face.

I'm sketching out the small rivet details along door seams, then building the bull bar frame with vertical posts, top and middle bars, and slats, plus alternating chevron trim pieces rotated for the classic warning pattern on the top bar.

Now I'm designing the grille: a dark front face with vertical slats, plus a cyan accent strip positioned behind and slightly in front of the slats so it glows through the gaps.

For the headlights, I'm placing white glowing boxes with dark bezels behind them, adding magenta DRL strips below, and angling the hood corners so the hood (narrower than the cab) and headlights line up properly at roughly x ±0.95-1.2.
